# unifi_wan_sla (Resource)

Manage a WAN SLA (Settings > Internet > WAN SLA): the monitors that decide whether a WAN counts as up for failover and load balancing. Uses the Network application's v2 API (`/v2/api/site/<site>/wan-slas`), which the integration API does not cover. A WAN refers to its SLA by ID (`wan_sla` on the WAN); this resource doesn't change which WAN uses which SLA. The monitor list is authoritative and numbered in order. Import with `<site_id>/<sla_id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "unifi_site" "default" {
  name = "Default"
}

# Fail over when a quarter of the pings to 1.1.1.1 are lost, or they take
# 500 ms, over one minute: a single lost ping doesn't switch the WAN.
resource "unifi_wan_sla" "primary" {
  site_id             = data.unifi_site.default.id
  name                = "ping 1.1.1.1"
  monitor_health_type = "ALL"
  monitors = [{
    type              = "ICMP"
    target            = "1.1.1.1"
    interval          = 1
    time_period       = 60
    loss_threshold    = 25
    latency_threshold = 500
    threshold_policy  = "any"
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `monitors` (Attributes List) The probes, in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors))
- `name` (String) Name shown in the UI.
- `site_id` (String) Integration site UUID.

### Optional

- `monitor_health_type` (String) How the monitors combine: `ALL` (the WAN is down when every monitor fails), `ANY` (when one fails), `MAJORITY` (three or more monitors) or `CUSTOM`. Keeps the controller's value when not set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The SLA's ID, as a WAN's `wan_sla` refers to it.

<a id="nestedatt--monitors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors`

Required:

- `interval` (Number) Seconds between probes.
- `threshold_policy` (String) Which exceeded thresholds fail the monitor, for example `any` (one is enough) or `all`.
- `time_period` (Number) Seconds of probes the thresholds are evaluated over.
- `type` (String) `ICMP` pings `target`; `DNS` resolves `domain` through the server `target`.

Optional:

- `domain` (String) Name to resolve, for `DNS` monitors.
- `jitter_threshold` (Number) Jitter in milliseconds at which the monitor fails. Not set: not evaluated.
- `latency_threshold` (Number) Latency in milliseconds at which the monitor fails. Not set: not evaluated.
- `loss_threshold` (Number) Packet loss in percent (0-100) at which the monitor fails. Not set: not evaluated.
- `target` (String) Host to ping, or the DNS server to ask; required for both types.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the integration site UUID and the SLA's ID (a WAN's `wan_sla`).
terraform import unifi_wan_sla.primary <site_id>/<sla_id>
```
